name: Cartesian tree monotone-stack construction
definition: For ordered keys K_i=(x_i,i) and indices 0≤i<n, initialize left_i=right_i=⊥ and stack S empty. For each i in increasing order set p=⊥; while S is nonempty and K_top>K_i set p=pop(S). Set left_i=p; if S remains nonempty set right_top=i; push i. The root is the bottom of S, or ⊥ if n=0.
variables: n array length; i zero-based index; x_i comparable value; K_i lexicographic value/index key; left_i,right_i child pointers; S right-spine stack; p last removed node; ⊥ null sentinel
assumptions: Finite immutable indexed array; values admit a consistent total ordering; compare by value and then increasing index to resolve equal values; child pointers initially null; sequential construction
limitations: O(n) comparisons, pointer operations and auxiliary storage under constant-cost indexing and comparisons; a single insertion can cost O(n). Output may be highly unbalanced. Construction alone supplies neither constant-time range queries nor a dynamic update structure
failure_conditions: Reject unordered values or inconsistent comparators, invalid indices and non-null stale child pointers
Do not interpret an empty tree as a valid range minimum; changes to the input invalidate the static structure
computation: Scan indices left to right; remove the right-spine suffix with greater keys, attach the last removed node as the new left subtree, attach the new node as the surviving top's right child if present, then push. Return the root and child arrays.

source.citation: Demaine (2012), MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, Lecture 15, sections 2.1–2.1.1, pp. 2–4. https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-851-advanced-data-structures-spring-2012/99d1ee86e7c3488b9a47174160776405_MIT6_851S12_L15.pdf

application: General ordered-array tree construction and reduction of leftmost range minima to lowest common ancestor queries; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite array of consistently ordered keys and fresh child-pointer storage.
incompatible_methods: Treating the constructed tree alone as an efficient lowest-common-ancestor query engine
mechanism_note: The stack holds the increasing-key right spine. Replacing its popped suffix by the new node with the displaced subtree on the left preserves in-order index order and strict lexicographic heap order. These properties uniquely determine the tree by its minimum root and recursive subarrays. Each node is pushed once and popped at most once. Unlike a sliding-window deque, this construction retains child topology for all indices; unlike a sparse table it constructs an ordered tree rather than storing overlapping aggregates. Deterministic leftmost tie resolution is a specified convention.

name: Binary lifting tree ancestor query
definition: For a rooted tree of n≥1 nodes let P(root)=⊥ and P(⊥)=⊥; J=max(1,ceil(log₂ n)). Set T_{0,v}=P(v), T_{j,v}=T_{j−1,T_{j−1,v}} for 1≤j<J and T_{j,⊥}=⊥. For valid node v and integer k≥0, return ⊥ if k≥n; otherwise start w=v and for each set bit j of k set w=T_{j,w}. Return w.
variables: n tree size; v,w nodes; P immediate parent; ⊥ missing ancestor sentinel; J number of levels; T jump table; j bit position; k upward edge distance
assumptions: Static connected rooted tree with a unique parent for every nonroot and no cycles; root has no parent; exact nonnegative integer distance and valid node indices; sentinel is outside node domain
limitations: O(n log(n+1)) preprocessing and storage and O(log(n+1)) query time under constant-cost indexing and bounded integer operations. If k exceeds depth, return missing ancestor, not the root. Structural changes or rerooting invalidate the table; no constant-time or optimal-space claim
failure_conditions: Reject malformed parent maps, invalid node identifiers, negative or noninteger distances and inconsistent jump dimensions
Never index the table with an unmapped missing ancestor or out-of-range bit; reject stale preprocessing
computation: Validate the parent tree, initialize immediate-parent row including absorbing sentinel, then fill each higher row by composing the preceding row with itself. For k=0 return v; for k≥n return missing; otherwise apply set-bit jumps with sentinel propagation.

source.citation: Demaine (2012), MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, Lecture 15, sections 1.3 and 4.2 (Algorithm B), pp. 2 and 7, CSAIL scribed notes. https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.851/fall17/scribe/lec15.pdf

application: General static tree ancestor lookup by edge distance; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Validated static rooted tree parent map, node identifier and nonnegative integer ancestor distance.
incompatible_methods: Clamping absent ancestors to the root when missing-ancestor semantics are required
Reusing a jump table after rerooting without rebuilding
mechanism_note: By induction T_{j,v}=P^{2^j}(v), extending P by an absorbing missing sentinel. Function composition adds iteration counts, so the binary expansion of k gives exactly P^k(v). Tree depth is at most n−1; the early large-distance check prevents missing levels. This is repeated parent-function composition, not overlapping range aggregation or union-find compression; it is not itself a lowest-common-ancestor algorithm. The source's section 4 height-difference notation is not used because height differences in branching trees need not equal edge distance.
